plugins.name: pm
plugins.description: DataCraft PM, the hands-on way of working: outcome-sized tickets, one session per outcome by default, nested sessions the main session manages for independent tickets, opt-in orchestration with up to six subagents, proportionate verification, delivery acceptance and concise handoffs. Also carries what the sdlc and ui-test plugins used to: the credential guard (a PreToolUse hook that blocks staging or committing credential-shaped files), gate-hooks (one gate script in a repo's .claude/: production gate, protected paths, a test lock for fix tasks, a commit and Stop backstop), review-policy with its read-only policy-reviewer agent, and ui-test (agent-run UI tests for macOS apps: a Codex computer-use runner under Ringer, executed checks on the receipt, a separate verifier). Also Runway, the unattended ticket loop (engine in runway/, plus the runway skill), folded in from the factory plugin at 0.26.0. Its Codex edition carries the credential guard, ui-test and runway, not gate-hooks or review-policy. Existing project requirements and permissions remain binding.

plugins.name: pm-sp
plugins.description: pm on Superpowers: Joe's PM layer around a trimmed, vendored copy of obra/superpowers (brainstorming with visuals, plans run in one session by subagents, branch finishing, TDD, debugging) without its session-start hook, plus Matt Pocock's wayfinder, grilling, domain-modeling, codebase-design, prototype, research and pr. Adds whats-next / stepping-away / checkpoint, nested-sessions for plan lanes, second-opinion (Sol via Ringer plus a fresh Opus), ship-acceptance, the credential guard, gate-hooks, review-policy and ui-test. Install instead of pm, never alongside it; needs no other plugin.

plugins.name: pm-runway
plugins.description: pm-sp plus unattended tickets, in one plugin (source of truth: the public runway-agent repo, pm-runway/). Everything pm-sp has, our own versions of Matt Pocock's to-spec, to-tickets and implement-spec (plus his tdd and code-review), and Runway on Orca: tickets as files, a plain-script loop that starts each build and review as a fresh Orca worker on whichever Mac is free, the reviewer always a different agent from the builder, work moved to the other agent when a subscription hits its usage limit, one branch per chunk gated once to main, a board page and runway-ask to ask what's happening. Uses your own Claude Code and Codex CLI sign-ins; Ringer optional. Install instead of pm-sp or pm, never alongside them.

plugins.name: design-dc
plugins.description: DataCraft design workflow: design-handoff (the crossing brief for claude.ai/design), html-artifacts (rich editorial HTML instead of long markdown), excalidraw-artifacts (HTML artifact → locked Excalidraw markup canvas, and annotation readback), design-sync (component-library sync via the built-in DesignSync tool). Pairs with the separate claude-design bridge plugin.

plugins.name: fm-dc
plugins.description: Agentic FileMaker development: SaXML patching with verify/rollback, DDR analysis, snippet validation, server-connection doctrine, and project scaffolding. Commands /fm-dc:fm-init, fm-scaffold, fm-status, fm-rollback, fm-docs-sync.

plugins.name: fm-lens
plugins.description: FM Lens (source of truth: the private FM_Agent_Lens repo, lens/): agentic FileMaker development on machines with the Claris Agentic Development Toolkit (ADT). Ships the FM Lens FileMaker plug-in, an agent's eyes and hands inside FileMaker Pro: window and web viewer snapshots, state probes, menus, go-to-layout, dialog handling, the XML clipboard and a drop-folder command channel. Its skills fill what Claris's ADT plugin leaves out: native layout rendering traps, the per-build capability list, the master quirks list, connection lifecycle and unwedge playbook, and filemaker (fm) CLI field notes. Install alongside Claris's filemaker-agentic-development plugin, INSTEAD of fm-dc.

plugins.name: agenticdev-filemaker-standards
plugins.description: The agenticdev Claris ADT standards pack (naming, patterns, advisory; prose only, as ADT 0.9 reads no checks file) — the house FileMaker conventions fm-lens points at. Install, then run `adt standards use agenticdev` in the project. Source of truth is standards/pack in the private FM_Agent_Lens repo; this entry only points at it.

plugins.name: basecamp-dc
plugins.description: Basecamp client-face layer, opt-in per repo via .basecamp/config.json (inert without it; pm never depends on it). bc-client-face carries the conventions — client's side (New requests, Questions for you) and Joe's side (Shipped / Active / Backlog as the status), Work items as clusters with Ref footers, [bc:<id>] tokens in TASKS.md, the plain-copy rule every Basecamp write is swept against, quirk safety rules; bc-close-out ships a task (move to Shipped unchecked, comment, prepend to What shipped without duplicating images); a session-start hook surfaces the project when the config is present. Works through the official basecamp CLI (0.12.0+) or the Basecamp connector, whichever the machine has.
